posts.content_md:
Hey, not sure what you mean by faster? I cook my emulsion for about an hour all together, of which time I am cleaning the glass. Then it takes me another 1/2 hour to 1 hour to coat. Yesterday I coated 12 - 5 x 7's and 8 4 x 5's. Half with Knox and half with Type A gelatin(250 bloom). I tried the bone so I figured it was time to try the Type A. It took my 2 1/2 hours all together but I was playing with the laser while waiting and cooked real low, slow and long.

So, have you had a chance to make any holograms with your latest batch of plates yet?

> **DannyBruza:** coated 15 5x7 plates 5 4x5 in 45 mins in dcg....and packed away to age for a day

I am still very anxious to see how your DCG emulsion performed holographically. Did you get a chance to make any hologram with these yet or did the wave plate set back all your holographing? I know how much work goes into making plates and it would be a shame to waste them. At the least, use the viewing method described here with shining a spatially filtered HeNe through the standard DCG plates and look at the thru beam on the wall. You will be amazed.
